design_critique:
1) The revision changes only kp (6 to 7) against iteration 1, but the evidence for the direction is weak. Between iteration 0 and iteration 1, max_error on the oval rose from 0.0643 to 0.0665 when ki, kd and base_speed were all cut, so the peak excursions moved with the gains, not against them. That result is compatible with kp being too low, but it is equally compatible with the peaks being set by something the design does not change. The kp step is a guess, not a tested mechanism.
2) The off-track limit is 0.06 m, and max_error is 0.0625 on the s-bend, 0.0643 on the slalom and 0.0665 on the oval. The rationale cites only the oval and slalom, and leaves out that the s-bend also exceeds the limit. Every track fails the same margin, so the fix has to be general, not tuned to one shape.
3) The 25 mm tape and the sensor span (x = -0.024 to +0.024, footprints 0.016 m) mean the line is seen out to about 0.044 m offset. The robot leaves the track at 0.06 m, so the sensors cannot see the line in the 0.044 to 0.06 band. Once an excursion passes about 0.044 m, the controller is steering from last_direction or a single outer sensor. The revision does not address this gap, and kp alone cannot fix a loss of sensing. Line losses of 1 to 2 per run are consistent with this, and the rationale does not test it.
4) rms_error of 0.025 to 0.030 m is not small. It is roughly twice the 0.0125 m half-tape width and about half the 0.06 m limit. The robot is not tracking the centre closely on average, so calling it 'tracking well' overstates the data. A higher kp may increase steering_oscillation (0.14 to 0.21) without lowering rms_error.
5) Speed is internally inconsistent. Iteration 1 changed base_speed from 1.5 to 1.4. Oval progress rose from 0.2275 to 0.244, so the slower speed did not reduce progress. The revision keeps 1.4 and says 'cutting it further would lower average speed toward the 1.5 m/s the finish needs', but 1.4 is already below 1.5. No run has finished, and completion_time has never been measured, so the 3 s deadline remains untested. This is the largest term in the score (500 points) and the design has no plan for it.
6) The controller is still at ki 0.1 and kd 0.3, and the revision does not test whether ki is too small to hold the robot through sustained bends, the other likely cause of off-track peaks.
rationale_critique:
1) The 'single change' framing is only partly true. Relative to iteration 1 it is one change, but the rationale's pre-stated rule (raise kp by 1 if max_error stays above 0.06) was set before any evidence that kp limits the peaks. The rationale presents the rule as a test, yet the iteration-0 to iteration-1 data show gain changes moving max_error in both directions.
2) The hypotheses are numbers without derivation: max_error below 0.06 m, line_loss_events at 1 or fewer, progress above 0.25 on the oval. The rationale gives no reason kp 7 should lower line losses, and line losses are not linked to kp anywhere in the data.
3) The speed reasoning contradicts itself. It says 1.4 is kept so the robot does not fall below the 1.5 m/s the finish needs, which describes a rate the design does not reach. The completion risk is acknowledged in the critique but not in the hypotheses: the rationale does not predict whether any run will finish or what to do if completion_time is above 3 s.
4) 'Robot tracks well on average' conflicts with the rms_error values, which are about twice the tape half-width. The rationale should say the average offset is large and that the failure is in the tails.
5) The fallback rule for steering_oscillation (if it rises more than 50 percent, drop kd to 0.1 to 0.2 instead of raising kd) is reasonable, but it does not say what happens if line losses stay at 2 or more. The search_right test is named as the next step, but it is not stated whether that test would change the design or only be measured.
6) The rationale does not state what the score change should be if the design still does not finish. With 0 finishes in both iterations, the score (about 65) comes almost entirely from progress, so the rationale should say how a progress gain would be judged, not only whether max_error falls.
